rule_description: order_id must not be blank or null.
evidence_summary: 0 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A missing order_id would make an order row unjoinable and uncountable in any downstream fact table.

rule_description: order_id must not repeat across orders.csv rows.
evidence_summary: 24 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Duplicate order_id values can double-count revenue and break one-to-one joins with payments.

rule_description: order_ts must not be blank or null.
evidence_summary: 1 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A missing order timestamp prevents freshness checks and any time-based reporting for the order.

rule_name: order_ts must parse as a valid timestamp
rule_description: order_ts must parse as a valid date-time value.
evidence_summary: 5 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: An unparseable timestamp cannot be ordered chronologically or used in any date-based KPI.

rule_description: order_ts must not be later than the fixed profiling reference date (2026-10-14).
evidence_summary: 7 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Future-dated orders distort daily/weekly revenue trends and freshness metrics if treated as real transactions.

rule_description: customer_id must not be blank or null.
evidence_summary: 18 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Whether guest/anonymous checkout is allowed determines if these orders can be used for customer-level reporting.

rule_description: product_id must match a product_id present in products.csv.
evidence_summary: 9 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: An order referencing an unknown product cannot be enriched with category, brand, or price for reporting.

rule_description: store_id must match a store_id present in stores.csv.
evidence_summary: 5 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: An order referencing an unknown store cannot be attributed to a zone/area for store-level reporting.

rule_name: quantity must be greater than zero
rule_description: quantity must be a positive number.
evidence_summary: 10 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Negative amounts were also observed alongside non-positive quantities, which directly affects revenue and margin totals.

rule_description: discount_pct must fall within the 0-100 range.
evidence_summary: 3 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A discount outside 0-100 makes the order_amount formula produce a nonsensical result.

rule_name: order_amount must match the business formula
rule_description: order_amount must equal quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100), rounded to 2 decimals.
evidence_summary: 18 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A formula mismatch means the recorded revenue for the order cannot be trusted without investigation.

rule_name: order_status must be in the approved list
rule_description: order_status must be one of ['CANCELLED', 'DELIVERED', 'RETURNED'].
evidence_summary: 5 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: An unapproved status value can be silently excluded from, or wrongly included in, status-based KPIs.

rule_name: payment_mode must be in the approved list
rule_description: payment_mode must be one of ['Card', 'Cash on Delivery', 'UPI', 'Wallet'].
evidence_summary: 10 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Unapproved values split payment-mode reporting; some (e.g. trailing-space 'UPI ') are safe to trim, others (e.g. 'Cashh') are suspicious spellings with no approved mapping yet.

rule_description: Every order with order_status = DELIVERED must have a non-blank delivery_minutes value.
evidence_summary: 8 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Delivery-time KPIs (including the 10-minute promise) silently undercount these DELIVERED orders.

rule_name: delivery_minutes must not exceed the approved threshold
rule_description: delivery_minutes must not exceed an approved SLA threshold (observed values go as high as 1440 minutes; no threshold is approved yet).
evidence_summary: 6 of 2412 orders.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Extreme delivery times distort average delivery time and the 10-minute promise KPI if left unflagged.

rule_description: payment_id must not repeat across payments.csv rows.
evidence_summary: 8 of 2228 payments.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Duplicate payment_id values can double-count settled revenue during reconciliation.

rule_name: payment order_id must exist in orders.csv
rule_description: payments.order_id must match an order_id present in orders.csv.
evidence_summary: 8 of 2228 payments.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A payment with no matching order cannot be reconciled against any order_amount and may represent lost or mismatched source data.

rule_name: SUCCESS payment amount must equal order_amount
rule_description: For payment_status = SUCCESS, amount_paid must equal the related order_amount (tolerance 0.01).
evidence_summary: 14 of 2228 payments.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A mismatch between a successful payment and its order amount directly affects finance reconciliation.

rule_description: payment_ts must not be later than the fixed profiling reference date (2026-10-14).
evidence_summary: 7 of 2228 payments.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Future-dated payments distort daily settlement and reconciliation reporting if treated as real transactions.

rule_name: gateway_ref must be present for non-Cash-on-Delivery payments
rule_description: gateway_ref must not be blank when payment_mode is not Cash on Delivery.
evidence_summary: 0 of 2228 payments.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A missing gateway reference on an electronic payment would prevent settlement tracing with the payment gateway; Cash on Delivery payments are expected to have none.

rule_name: customer_id must be unique in customers.csv
rule_description: customer_id must not repeat across customers.csv rows.
evidence_summary: 10 of 405 customers.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Duplicate customer_id values (with differing phone/area/pincode) make it unclear which contact details are current for that customer.

rule_description: city should be populated for every customer.
evidence_summary: 6 of 405 customers.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: City-level reporting undercounts customers with a blank city, though the record may still load.

rule_description: signup_date must not be later than the fixed profiling reference date (2026-10-14).
evidence_summary: 3 of 405 customers.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A future signup_date is implausible and may indicate a source-system timestamp problem, but it does not affect revenue.

rule_name: loyalty_tier must be in the approved list
rule_description: loyalty_tier must be one of {Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum}; casing variants (e.g. BRONZE, bronze, SILVER) should be standardised to the approved spelling.
evidence_summary: 8 of 405 customers.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Casing variants split loyalty-tier reporting into extra groups unless standardised to the approved spelling.

rule_name: product_id must be unique in products.csv
rule_description: product_id must not repeat across products.csv rows.
evidence_summary: 4 of 152 products.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A reused product_id for a renamed/re-priced '(old)' variant makes it ambiguous which name/price applies to historical orders.

rule_description: category should be populated for every product.
evidence_summary: 3 of 152 products.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Category-level reporting undercounts products with a blank category, though the record may still load.

rule_name: mrp must be greater than zero
rule_description: mrp must be a positive number.
evidence_summary: 1 of 152 products.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A zero or negative retail price is not usable in any margin or revenue calculation involving this product.

rule_description: cost_price should not be greater than mrp.
evidence_summary: 5 of 152 products.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: cost_price above mrp implies a negative gross margin on every sale, which needs catalog-team review.

rule_name: store_id must be unique in stores.csv
rule_description: store_id must not repeat across stores.csv rows.
evidence_summary: 0 of 15 stores.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: No duplicate store_id values currently exist; this safeguard rule prevents a future load from silently introducing one.

rule_description: zone should be populated for every store.
evidence_summary: 1 of 15 stores.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: Zone-level reporting undercounts stores with a blank zone, though the record may still load.

rule_name: capacity_orders_per_day must be greater than zero
rule_description: capacity_orders_per_day must be a positive number.
evidence_summary: 1 of 15 stores.csv rows fail this rule based on the Part 0 profiling evidence.
business_impact: A zero or negative daily capacity cannot be used in any store-level load-balancing or operations calculation.
